title: Multi-region entity synthesis and idempotent CRUD
content:
Purpose

Quick design notes on a control-plane data model and CRUD API approach that supports multi-region deployment, routing policies, and predictable idempotent behavior. This is exploratory — trying to capture a pragmatic set of primitives we can implement without a full distributed consensus stack.

Goals and constraints
- Single canonical API surface for hosted / dedicated / private control planes.
- Support multi-region resource binding (env -> region -> cluster) and region-local leases.
- Ensure CRUD semantics are idempotent and compatible with retries from clients and gateways.
- Allow routing policies to express locality, capacity tiers, and graceful fallback ordering.
- Keep runtime lookups cheap (small index per resource for route decision). Avoid large fanout on every request.
- Support offline deployments (private) where eventual convergence must be safe.

Key concepts (primitives)
- Resource: the top-level entity clients reference (e.g., model-deployment, endpoint, batch-queue).
  - resource_id: opaque globally unique id (uuid-ish). Prefer stable prefix: rsrc-<uuid>
  - resource_key: customer-visible name (project scoped), e.g., my-service/bert-latest
- Environment: logical grouping (dev, prod, canary) used for routing rules and quotas.
  - env_id: env-<name>-<tenant>
- Region: cloud region string (us-west1, eu-central1) where clusters exist.
- Cluster: concrete compute pool within a region (cluster_id). Clusters carry capacity/cost profile.
- Binding: a tuple linking resource -> environment -> region -> cluster with metadata (weight, priority, capacity_floor).
- RoutingPolicy: ordered rules over bindings (locality-first, then cost-tier, then spillover) with predicates.
- Record metadata: version (monotonic int or vector-clock-lite), created_at, last_modified, tombstone flag.

Canonical identity and ownership
- resource_id is the canonical primary key. All control plane writes supply either resource_id (for update/upsert) or resource_key + owner (create).
- Ownership: each record stores owner_id (tenant) and allowed editors. ACL enforcement happens at API gateway layer; control plane stores ACLs but does not do auth decision.

Resource record sketch (flat JSON-ish fields; keep small)
- resource_id: string
- resource_key: string
- owner_id: string
- env_bindings: list of binding ids or short objects (region, cluster, weight, priority, capacity_hint)
- routing_policy_id: string
- status: active | draining | deleted
- version: integer (bumped on each mutating write)
- last_modified: timestamp
- annotations: freeform short map (string->string) for operator labels

Notes on bindings representation
- We want cheap route decisions. Store env_bindings as a small list of region-level entries for typical fast lookup: [{region: us-west1, clusters: [{id:c1, weight:80},{id:c2,weight:20}], priority: 10}]
- For very large deployments we allow a cluster-set reference (refers to a cluster-group record) to avoid huge resource records.

Routing policy model (expressive but bounded)
- Policy is an ordered list of steps. Each step: predicate (e.g., same-region, within-cost-tier), selection strategy (weighted, priority), fallback pointer.
- Built-in predicates: same-region, same-country, same-cloud, low-latency, cost-tier<=N, capacity-available>=X
- Strategies: prefer-local, spread-weighted, prefer-cheapest, prefer-high-capacity
- Policies are declarative and small. Example: [step1: same-region prefer-local], [step2: cost-tier<=2 spread-weighted], [step3: fallback global cheapest]

CRUD API semantics (idempotent first-class)
- Create (POST /v1/resources)
  - If client supplies resource_id: treat as idempotent create-if-not-exists; return 409 only if resource_id exists but owner mismatch.
  - If client supplies resource_key without resource_id: server generates resource_id and returns it. Repeated creates with same resource_key+owner are idempotent for a short window (5m) via a create-token we return; otherwise create new if after TTL.
- Read (GET /v1/resources/{resource_id})
  - Returns latest stable version, plus version metadata for optimistic concurrency.
- Update (PATCH /v1/resources/{resource_id})
  - Support conditional update semantics: if_version=N header or version field. If mismatch -> 412. This keeps optimistic concurrency cheap.
  - All updates must be idempotent: clients should include a client-op-id for retry de-duplication. Control plane stores last client-op-id per resource for short retention (e.g., 24h).
- Upsert
  - Support PUT semantics that are idempotent and either create or replace. Must include owner metadata to avoid accidental cross-tenant takeovers.
- Delete (DELETE /v1/resources/{resource_id})
  - Soft delete by default: set tombstone + status=deleted and bump version. Actual GC is asynchronous and gated by tenant/retention policy.
  - Deletion is idempotent. If delete called again, return 200 and current tombstone state.

Idempotency and dedupe strategy
- Every mutating call accepts client_op_id (uuid) and optional idempotency-key header.
- Control plane keeps a small persistent dedupe window per resource: last_op_id->result (status, resource_version, timestamp) for 24h.
- Read-after-write consistency: on resources owned by single-tenant control plane we can offer strongly consistent reads. For global multi-master private deployments we provide read-your-writes per-client using client_op_id hints and local lease reads.

Multi-region synthesis and conflict resolution
- Avoid multi-master per-record MVCC. Prefer single-writer per-resource pattern where the canonical writer is the control-plane instance in the resource's primary region.
- Primary region selection: derived from owner tenant preference -> env binding -> explicit primary_region. If primary region absent, pick home region (tenant default) and record it.
- Writes outside of primary are proxied to primary when possible. If offline, allow queued writes with version conflict detection on re-sync.
- Conflict resolution rule: last-writer-wins on version number. To avoid generative surprises, require monotonically increasing client-supplied intent_id sequence for brokers doing offline write batching.

Cluster-level leases and ephemeral state
- Do not store capacity counters in the resource record. Use cluster leases (separate short-lived records) for scheduling decisions. Leases managed by cluster agents and referenced by binding entries.
- Binding entries carry capacity_hint that cluster agents reconcile with actual capacity via telemetry.

Query patterns and indexing
- Most runtime lookups are: given (resource_id, environment, client_region) return ordered cluster list + routing policy.
- Maintain a small materialized view keyed by (resource_id, env, region) to avoid scanning env_bindings at request time. This view is updated by control plane writes and can be sharded by resource_id.

Migration / backfill notes
- Existing control-plane records may have cluster lists that are region-centric. Backfill should synthesize cluster-group refs where >N clusters exist.
- We will run a pass to compute primary_region for legacy records without one. Default to tenant default, log metrics for manual review.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Strong vs eventual consistency: for internal-only control planes, strong consistency is fine; for customer-private multi-master we need an explicit offline-first flow and merge semantics.
- Version format: plain integer vs hybrid logical clock. Integers are simplest; consider hybrid clock if cross-region offline writes are common.
- TTLs for dedupe cache (24h vs 7d) — operational cost vs client convenience.
- How to express complex rollouts (A/B, weighted canary) in small routing policies without bloating policy eval cost.

Action items
- Prototype API surface (POST/GET/PATCH/PUT/DELETE) with idempotency-key and client_op_id support. (Owner: Marco)
- Implement a small materialized view service for (resource_id, env, region) queries (Owner: Noor)
- Draft migration tool to compute primary_region for legacy records and replace large cluster lists with cluster-group refs (Owner: Aisha)
- RFC on dedupe retention and versioning strategy (Owner: Rahul)

Notes-to-self
- Keep payloads small. Avoid full cluster lists on hot-path reads if possible. Materialized view + cluster-group refs are essential.
- Make API behavior clear for private deployments in docs: how offline writes are handled and what guarantees we provide.
- Test failure scenarios: proxying writes to primary failing, queued write replay, and client-op-id replay after GC of dedupe cache.

End of notes
